subject: note-update-semantics
detail: A's PUT sets only title and body; B's PUT merges the whole request body into the note (Object.assign), so a client can overwrite id, pinned or labels
solutions: Whitelist title and body on update; pin/unpin and tags through their own endpoints
recommended: Whitelist title and body; reject unknown fields with 400

subject: labels-to-tags
detail: B stores labels as a free-text array per note (duplicates allowed); the kept model is A's shared, uniquely named tags. Migrating labels collapses duplicates and case variants
solutions: Map each distinct trimmed, case-folded label to one tag and link it
recommended: Map labels to tags (trim, case-fold, de-duplicate); log merged variants

subject: jotter-data-in-memory
detail: B keeps notes only in process memory, so there is no stored B data to migrate; any live B data can only be captured from a running instance before it stops
solutions: Treat B as having no data to migrate
Capture a running instance's GET /api/notes output (needs approval to run or call it)
recommended: Plan the B import from a JSON dump of GET /api/notes; if none exists, B has no data to migrate

subject: export-filenames
detail: B names export files <title>.md, so equal titles collide and titles with / or other unsafe characters produce bad paths
solutions: Slugify title and append a short id
recommended: Slugify title plus first 8 characters of the uuid
